tasks.title: Classify a failed preprocess read with a Python re-read (_read_failure)
tasks.test_approach: Unit tests of the helper on real files in tmp_path. Forcing method (no builtins patch): write a garbage file so SimpleITK fails, then monkeypatch.setattr(pre, 'open', raiser, raising=False) so only preprocess's own open raises. A spy (monkeypatch pre._read_failure) for A6. TDD: each test red first. The raiser is path-selective: it raises only when the path is the garbage file and otherwise returns builtins.open(...), so series.csv and other reads are untouched. Forced-error variants run with workers=1 (a monkeypatch does not reach a spawned worker).
criteria: preprocess has one helper _read_failure(path), called by read_image and read_info only after quiet_call raised CaseRefused, after the except block (read_series's shape), then the CaseRefused is raised

_read_failure opens the file with the bare builtin open(path, 'rb') (binary mode; not Path.open or os.open, so the module-level patch reaches it) and reads it in fixed-size chunks to the end outside quiet_call; it returns on a clean read
_read_failure returns (swallows) on FileNotFoundError
_read_failure raises MemoryError when dicom_io.allocation_failure(exc) is true for the OSError (ENOMEM)
_read_failure re-raises any other OSError (e.g. PermissionError, EIO)
A3 unit: a FileNotFoundError from the Python read keeps read_image's CaseRefused(REASON_FILE_UNREADABLE)
A3b unit: a forced PermissionError from the Python read makes read_image and read_info raise that OSError; a forced ENOMEM OSError raises MemoryError (runs as root too)
A2 unit: a truncated or garbage NIfTI still raises CaseRefused(REASON_FILE_UNREADABLE) from read_image and read_info
A6: when SimpleITK succeeds, _read_failure is not called (spy)
A MemoryError already raised by quiet_call (an allocation failure) does not call _read_failure
The MemoryError for ENOMEM is raised bare after the except block: its __context__ and __cause__ are None (no path-naming OSError attached)

read_image's and read_info's docstrings say a file-system error from the re-read propagates as OSError (and ENOMEM as MemoryError); only a malformed or vanished file is CaseRefused(REASON_FILE_UNREADABLE)

tasks.title: Patient-level I/O error through preprocess(); spec table row
tasks.test_approach: End-to-end preprocess() runs on synthetic converted trees (write_plan, add_series with reg_matrix='identity', report_rows). Real chmod 0 is skipped as root (skipif os.geteuid() == 0, as tests/test_dicom_io.py). Forcing method (no builtins patch): write a garbage file so SimpleITK fails, then monkeypatch.setattr(pre, 'open', raiser, raising=False) so only preprocess's own open raises. Every chmod test also has a forced-PermissionError variant that runs as root. The raiser is path-selective: it raises only when the path is the garbage file and otherwise returns builtins.open(...), so series.csv and other reads are untouched. Forced-error variants run with workers=1 (a monkeypatch does not reach a spawned worker).
criteria: A1: a plan file with read permission removed gives exactly one patient-level REASON_IO_ERROR row for that patient and no plan rows; a second patient in the same run is preprocessed
A1 variant: the same outcome with a garbage file plus a forced PermissionError from preprocess's open (runs as root)
A3: a file named in series.csv but missing still refuses its plan with REASON_FILE_MISSING (the existing test passes, or one new test if none exists)
A4: a registered series with a valid reg matrix whose file has read permission removed gives the patient's REASON_IO_ERROR
A4 variant: the same outcome for the registered series with a garbage file plus a forced PermissionError (runs as root)

A5 (forced-PermissionError setup, so it runs as root): with workers=1, no caplog record and no text of preprocess_report.csv contains the unreadable file's path; the patient folder name appears only in the report's patient column
A7: the existing manifest tests pass unchanged
docs/specs/2026-11-03-f2b-preprocess.md's error table gains a row: a file-system error while reading an input -> patient row refused, REASON_IO_ERROR
README's troubleshooting or report notes say a disk or permission error while reading an input fails the whole patient with the I/O-error reason
